four equal charges on the seam circle, interacting through the kernel 1/(4 pi d): the only equilibrium reached from 60 random starts is the square (marks at mu_4)
without the reflection (free on the sphere) the equilibrium is the regular tetrahedron, with lower energy than the square
square: cross ratio harmonic, j = 1728 (square torus tau = i); tetrahedron: equianharmonic, j = 0 (hexagonal torus)
on the sphere the square is a saddle (energy falls when alternate marks leave the plane): it is stable only with the reflection, as recorded for tau = i in P1KERN20261119
consistency with the record: hexagon excluded by alpha (recorded alpha^-1 = 104.42), square needs the reflection; here the same two shapes appear as the two equilibria of the kernel
pairing sum of the Coulomb kernel over the three pairings on a rectangle with half angle theta: 1/4 + 1/sin^2(2 theta); at the square exactly 5/4
the same sum is 3 for the flat seed channel (the count in delta_top = 3 w^4) and 5/4 for the full Coulomb kernel at the square; 9/16 for 1/d^2, 9/8 at the tetrahedron
pattern only: 5/4 is also the fixed exponent B gamma = (3/2)(5/6) and delta_2/delta_top^2; no step turns a pairing sum into the exponent of (1 - q), so this is not a derivation

verdict C: mark position is no longer a free input under the reading: reflection (marks on the seam) plus the kernel's own repulsion gives mu_4; the premise 'marks carry equal charge and repel through the kernel' is new and not in the original

data.verdict: A: gauge potential not kernel data in the original. B: delta_top = three pairings of four marks at the damping variance; phi_base not explained. C: marks at mu_4 are the Coulomb equilibrium on the seam circle; 5/4 as pairing sum is a pattern.
